body: I do not think 13.1.1 as is today properly addresses the problem that base URL classes do not always do proper URL parsing. This impacts SSRF, Unvalidated Redirects, OAuth, SAML and more.

comments.body: updating libs is the best defense, letting this one go

@jmanico Is there any plan for updates of [13.1.1](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x21-V13-API.md#v131-generic-web-service-security)?
> Verify that all application components use the same encodings and parsers to avoid parsing attacks that exploit different URI or file parsing behavior that could be used in SSRF and RFI attacks.

So I think what Jim means is that generally it will be a library performing the parsers and that this issue generally relates to bugs in those parsers.

There is a good overview of bugs related to these sort of parsers in this report here (which also draws heavily on work from [Orange Tsai](https://www.blackhat.com/docs/us-17/thursday/us-17-Tsai-A-New-Era-Of-SSRF-Exploiting-URL-Parser-In-Trending-Programming-Languages.pdf) and [Daniel Stenberg](https://github.com/bagder/docs/blob/master/URL-interop.md)):
https://claroty.com/team82/research/exploiting-url-parsing-confusion

title: 13.1.1 does not fully address problem with bad URL parsers
